The claim depended on assuming exact-path semantics that the framework does not use. The related fail-open in tenantFor is reported separately at reduced confidence.

ruled_out.assertion: jwt.decode is called on the bearer token without verification, allowing a forged jti
ruled_out.killed_by: The same token was verified at line 30 and the request would already have been rejected; decode is used only to lift a correlation id for the access log. The mitigation is real and the comment describes it accurately.

ruled_out.assertion: legacyLookup queries invoices with an empty tenant id, enabling cross-tenant reads
ruled_out.killed_by: Private method, no caller anywhere in the tree (grepped), and tenant_id = '' matches no row in a table whose rows always carry a tenant. Not an intrinsic flaw under rule 08 either.

ruled_out.assertion: CORS is misconfigured because credentials are enabled alongside a configurable origin list
ruled_out.killed_by: allowedOrigins explicitly filters out '*' (`s !== '*'`) and defaults to a single https origin, so credentials are never paired with a wildcard. The mitigation works as written.

ruled_out.assertion: SSRF in the Open Graph preview endpoint
ruled_out.killed_by: The handler requires protocol === 'https:' and membership in a closed ALLOWED_PREVIEW_HOSTS set, uses redirect: 'manual' so it will not follow a redirect off the allowlist, and returns only the hostname and a length-bounded title. The mitigation is effective for the claimed class.

ruled_out.assertion: constantTimeEquals returns early on a length mismatch, leaking the workspace secret's length
ruled_out.killed_by: Length disclosure of a high-entropy stored secret is not a directly triggerable flaw, and the byte comparison itself is constant time. This is paranoia about an otherwise-correct primitive.

ruled_out.assertion: The KV rate limiter's read-modify-write is racy, so a client can exceed MAX_PER_WINDOW
ruled_out.killed_by: Rule 07: a request-budget module is not a DoS-defence primitive whose stated purpose is to withstand this, and the impact is bounded to exceeding a soft quota.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal in the settlement backfill's resolve_export
ruled_out.killed_by: candidate is fully resolved with Path.resolve() before the check, and `root not in candidate.parents` rejects both ../ escapes and symlinks pointing outside the drop root (resolve follows them first). The containment check is correct as written.

ruled_out.killed_by: No caller anywhere in the tree (grepped); the module's live path uses hmac.compare_digest at line 22. Rule 08's no-caller exemption does not apply: a plain string comparison helper is not a broken cryptographic primitive or a hardcoded secret.
Rule 02: the response contains only {'status': 'ok'} and nothing account-scoped; the comment documents the cross-origin status page that requires it.

ruled_out.assertion: The intake service reads request['org_id'] from an auth middleware that build_app never installs, so org scoping is absent
ruled_out.killed_by: build_app does indeed install no middleware, but aiohttp raises KeyError on the missing key, producing a 500 before anything is published. The behaviour fails closed, so there is no triggerable security flaw - it is a deployment/wiring defect.

findings.title: Raw SQL string interpolation of the search term in searchByMemo
findings.evidence: db.raw() parameterises tenant_id with a placeholder but splices the caller's term straight into the statement: `and memo ilike '%${term}%'`. term is the raw `q` query-string value from invoices.controller.ts:61-62 (`@Get('search') search(@Req() req, @Query('q') q = '')`), passed through with no escaping, quoting or length bound. Micro-harness: the template literal with q="%' union all select id, email, 0, password_hash from users --" produces a statement containing the attacker's UNION clause outside any quoted literal. Note also that the injected text sits before the parameter binding, so knex still binds tenant_id but the query shape is already attacker-chosen.
findings.impact: Any authenticated portal user can read or modify arbitrary rows in the billing database - other tenants' invoices, and any other table reachable by the pg role in DATABASE_URL - via GET /api/v1/invoices/search?q=. The tenant_id binding on the same statement provides no protection because the injection point is a separate predicate that can be terminated and followed by UNION/OR.
findings.recommendation: Bind the term: `and memo ilike ?` with `['%' + term + '%']`, or use the knex query builder (`.whereILike('memo', `%${term}%`)`). Escape LIKE metacharacters (% and _) in the term separately.

findings.title: Invoice detail cache is keyed on invoice id alone, so entries cross the tenant boundary
findings.evidence: `this.cache.wrap(`invoice:${invoiceId}`, () => this.repo.findForTenant(tenantId, invoiceId))`. The key omits tenantId while the loader is the only thing that applies the tenant filter, and TtlCache.wrap (common/cache.ts:16-24) returns the stored value without re-running the loader on a hit. The cache is a process-local Map shared by every request the replica serves, with a 30s TTL.
findings.impact: Once tenant A has fetched invoice X, any request for the same invoice id from tenant B within 30 seconds returns tenant A's row - the where({tenant_id}) clause is never evaluated. The inverse also holds: tenant B's miss caches `undefined` under the same key and denies the legitimate owner for the rest of the TTL. changeStatus invalidates the same unscoped key, so the defect is consistent rather than accidental.
findings.recommendation: Include the tenant in the key: `invoice:${tenantId}:${invoiceId}` (and update the invalidate call in changeStatus to match). Better, make TtlCache take a required scope argument so an unscoped key cannot be constructed.

findings.title: tenantFor falls open to a client-supplied tenant selector when no session is present

findings.title: /do/* forwards the client's request verbatim to the Durable Object, letting callers set their own X-Actor-Scopes
findings.evidence: LinkStore derives the caller's capabilities solely from the X-Actor-Scopes request header (do/LinkStore.ts:14-19), and its own comment says 'Scopes are stamped on by the router once it has authenticated the caller'. The /do/* branch builds `new Request(url, request)` - the second argument copies the original client request's headers - and hands it to stub.fetch() unchanged, so any header the client sent survives. The authenticated createLink path (handlers/links.ts:76) and the /api/links GET path (index.ts:118) do stamp the header from the session, which confirms the header is meant to be router-controlled.
findings.impact: A session holding only the viewer role (scopes: ['links:read']) can POST /do/put or /do/delete with `X-Actor-Scopes: links:admin` and pass every check in LinkStore.put/list/delete. Chained with the environment-gate bypass above, an unauthenticated caller reaches the same surface. /do/* is also outside LIMITED_PREFIXES (ratelimit.ts:9), so it is unmetered.
findings.recommendation: Strip and re-stamp identity headers on the forwarded request: build a fresh Headers object from the session rather than cloning the client's, e.g. `new Request(url, {method, body, headers: {'X-Actor-Scopes': session.scopes.join(',')}})`. Better, pass the scopes out-of-band (RPC method arguments) so a header can never carry authority.

findings.title: Attestation.verify never checks the signature and returns a tautology
findings.evidence: The function computes `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(...)` and returns `digest.isNotEmpty()`. The three preceding checks do not close the gap: blob.nonce must equal the nonce the service just handed out (obtainable from GET /api/devices/{serial}/nonce, which has no scope check), blob.certificateChainSha256 is compared against config.attestationRootFingerprint - a fixed public constant checked into application.conf:27 and supplied by the caller in the request - and blob.signature only has to be 64 characters long.

Any caller who can reach POST /api/devices/enroll can forge an AttestationBlob that passes: request a nonce for the target serial, echo it back with the published root fingerprint and 64 arbitrary characters. This is the sole control the enrolment path relies on, since that route performs no scope check either.
findings.recommendation: Verify the signature: load the manufacturing root's public key, validate the presented certificate chain against it, confirm the chain's fingerprint, and verify blob.signature over the serial||nonce message with the leaf key.
